sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好,这是6分钟英语 从英国广播公司学习英语。

sentences.en: I'm Phil. And I'm Becca. Sending emails is a big part of modern work, and most people try to write emails politely.
sentences.zh: 我是Phil,我是Becca 发送电子邮件是现代工作的一大部分, 大多数人都试着礼貌地写邮件。

sentences.en: Most, but not all! Recently, BBC Radio 4 programme All in the Mind asked listeners to tell them what they find rude in emails.
sentences.zh: 大部分,但并非全部! 最近英国广播公司第四电台节目《思想》要求听众在电子邮件中告诉他们他们觉得很粗鲁的东西。

sentences.en: Here, presenter Claudia Hammond and guest Pete Olusoga discuss what listeners had to say: Rachel in Manchester says what annoys her is people who start their emails with just your name and without a simple greeting like 'hi'.
sentences.zh: 在这里,主持人克劳迪娅·哈蒙德和嘉宾皮特·奥卢索加讨论听众们要说的话:曼彻斯特的瑞秋说,令她感到烦恼的是,人们开始用你的名字发邮件,而没有像“嗨”这样的简单的问候。

sentences.en: She says the unnecessary formality always has the effect of putting her immediately on the defensive.
sentences.zh: 她说不必要的手续 总是会立即让她处于防守状态

sentences.en: We've got an anonymous one here, who recently received a single emoji in response to a carefully considered and worded email.
sentences.zh: 我们这里有一个匿名的, 他最近收到一个单一的emoji 回应 仔细考虑和措辞的电子邮件。

sentences.en: One listener doesn't like emails which start with just her name because they put her on the defensive.
sentences.zh: 一位听众不喜欢用电子邮件 开始只用她的名字 因为他们让她处于防御状态

sentences.en: The phrase to put someone on the defensive means to do or say something which makes them feel threatened or unsure.
sentences.zh: 将某人置于防御手段上 来做或说点什么 让他们觉得受到威胁或不确定

sentences.en: Another listener found it rude when their email was answered with a single emoji, and I think that would annoy me too.
sentences.zh: 另一位听众在他们的电子邮件被用单张表解时觉得很粗鲁,

sentences.en: These emails are examples of people being uncivil – an adjective meaning rude or impolite.
sentences.zh: 这些电子邮件是人们不文明的例子 — — 一种形容词的意思是粗鲁或不礼貌。

sentences.en: And just to note, the noun that goes with this is incivility.
sentences.zh: 顺便提一下,这个名词是非文明的。

sentences.en: In this episode, we'll be hearing more about rude emails at work and, as usual, we'll be learning some useful new vocabulary, all of which you can find on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 和往常一样,我们会学习一些有用的新词汇, 这些都是你可以在我们网站上找到的,bbc学习英语.com。

sentences.en: But first, I have a question for you, Phil.
sentences.zh: 但首先 我有个问题要问你 菲尔

sentences.en: Last year, thousands of US government workers received an email requiring them to justify their job by listing five things they had accomplished that week… or resign.
sentences.zh: 去年,成千上万的美国政府工人收到一封电子邮件,要求他们通过列出他们那周完成的五件事情来证明其工作合理性.或辞职。

sentences.en: But who sent this email? Was it: a) Donald Trump, b) JD Vance, or c) Elon Musk?
sentences.zh: 但是谁发的邮件?

sentences.en: Ooh, I don't know... Maybe JD Vance? We'll find out later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 哦,我不知道,也许JD Vance?

sentences.en: Now, according to some psychologists, rudeness in emails is based on a fight-or-flight response humans feel when stressed.
sentences.zh: 根据一些心理学家的说法, 电子邮件中的粗鲁 是基于人类在压力下的反应。

sentences.en: Here, psychologist Dr Emma Russell explains these responses for BBC Radio 4's All in the Mind.
sentences.zh: 心理学家Emma Russell博士为BBC电台4频道的全心全意解释这些回应。

sentences.en: So, a fight response is usually when we try to dominate or belittle other people.
sentences.zh: 所以,战斗反应通常是当我们试图统治或贬低其他人的时候。

sentences.en: Emails that are hostile in tone and language, or even cc'ing senior personnel in on the message in order to elevate an issue and put someone in their place.
sentences.zh: 电子邮件在语气和语言上充满敌意, 或甚至让高层人员加入信息, 以便提升一个问题, 并让某人取代他们。

sentences.en: Then the flight response is when people try to protect themselves by withdrawing or avoiding.
sentences.zh: 那么飞行反应就是人们试图通过撤退或躲避来保护自己。

sentences.en: They won't reply, or if they do reply, maybe they don't answer all of the points in the email.
sentences.zh: 他们不会回答,或者如果他们回答, 也许他们不会回答邮件中的所有点。

sentences.en: They're just trying to get it off their plate.
sentences.zh: 他们只是想把它从盘子里弄出来

sentences.en: The fight response can make us belittle someone – make them feel inferior or unimportant.
sentences.zh: 战斗反应会让我们轻视某人, 让他们感到低劣或不重要。

sentences.en: For example, a boss sends a group email in which they give someone else the credit for the work you did.
sentences.zh: 例如,一个老板发了一个集体电子邮件 他们给别人的功劳 你的工作。

sentences.en: The boss wants to put you in your place – an idiom meaning to show someone that they are less important than they think they are.
sentences.zh: 上司想把你放在你的位置上 来向别人展示他们比他们想象的要不重要

sentences.en: The flight response, meanwhile, can be seen when co-workers ignore your message or give a quick, unhelpful reply.
sentences.zh: 同时,当同事无视你的信息或给予快速、无益的答复时,飞行反应就可以看到。

sentences.en: Such colleagues want to get work off their plate – another idiom, meaning to remove tasks from your own workload and give them to someone else to deal with.
sentences.zh: 这些同事想把工作从他们的盘子上移开, 换句话说, 换句话说,就是把工作从你自己的工作量中移开, 交给别人来处理。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, when stressed and working to a deadline it's hard to make sure all your emails are polite.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是,当压力和工作到一个最后期限 很难确保你所有的电子邮件是礼貌的。

sentences.en: That's what Emma Russell said when she spoke to BBC Radio 4's All in the Mind.
sentences.zh: Emma Russell在和BBC电台4号通话时也是这么说的

sentences.en: Because we're operating in these environments where we are all quite frazzled, we are more at risk of engaging in incivility.
sentences.zh: 因为我们在这种环境里工作 我们都非常疲惫, 我们更可能参与文明。

sentences.en: We're more likely to be uncivil when we're frazzled – an informal adjective describing feeling tired or anxious because you're doing too many things at the same time.
sentences.zh: 当我们疲惫的时候,我们更可能不文明 一种非正式的形容词 描述你感到疲倦或焦虑 因为你同时做太多的事情

sentences.en: Luckily, there are ways to help. If you feel angry when writing an email, pause before you hit send.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是,有办法可以帮助。如果你在写电子邮件时感到愤怒,请在发送前先暂停。

sentences.en: One day it might save your friendship or even your job!
sentences.zh: 有一天它会拯救你的友谊 甚至你的工作!

sentences.en: OK. Becca, I'm going to politely ask you to please reveal the answer to your question.
sentences.zh: 贝卡,我礼貌地请你 说出你的问题的答案

sentences.en: Of course, Phil. I asked you who sent the email requiring workers to justify their employment or resign.
sentences.zh: 当然了 菲尔 我问你是谁发的邮件

sentences.en: I said that I thought it might have been JD Vance.
sentences.zh: 我说我以为可能是JD Vance干的

sentences.en: Well, we're not going to fire you, Phil, but you are wrong.
sentences.zh: 我们不会解雇你的 菲尔 但你错了

sentences.en: The correct answer was Elon Musk. OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learnt, starting with the idiom put someone on the defensive, meaning to make someone feel threatened or unsure.
sentences.zh: 正确的答案是伊隆·穆斯克。好吧。让我们回顾一下我们学到的词汇, 从语义开始,让某人处于防御状态, 意思是让某人感到受到威胁或不确定。

sentences.en: The adjective uncivil means impolite, and we have a similar noun that's incivility.
sentences.zh: 形容词不文明意味着不礼貌, 我们有一个类似的名词,这是不文明的。

sentences.en: To belittle someone means to make them feel inferior or unimportant.
sentences.zh: 贬低某人意味着 让他们感到低劣或不重要

sentences.en: If you put someone in their place, you show them that they're not as important as they think they are.
sentences.zh: 如果你让某人代替他们 你让他们知道 他们不像他们认为的那么重要

sentences.en: To get something off your plate means to give someone else a task or problem instead of dealing with it yourself.
sentences.zh: 离开你的盘子 意味着给别人一个任务或问题 而不是自己去处理

sentences.en: And finally, if you're frazzled, you feel tired or anxious because you're doing too much.
sentences.zh: 最后,如果你是疲惫的, 你感到疲倦或焦虑 因为你做太多。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up. If you want to know more about communication at work, check out our series Office English.
sentences.zh: 再说一遍,我们六分钟就到了。如果你想了解更多关于工作沟通的信息,请看看我们的英文系列节目。

sentences.en: It's on our website, along with a quiz and a worksheet for this episode, and that's bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 在我们的网站上,还有这个片段的测验和工作表, 这是bbc学习英语。com。

sentences.en: But now it's goodbye. Bye!
sentences.zh: 现在再见了 再见!
